headline: High Altitude Preparation and Seasonal Pass Check
reservation: No permits are required for town entry, but U.S. Forest Service campgrounds at Turquoise Lake require reservations through the national system up to six months ahead. Major race weekends in July and August cause local lodging to reach capacity; book early.

days.title: Historic Peaks and Mining Heritage

stops.name: Mineral Belt Trail
stops.detail: Cycle or walk this 11.6-mile paved loop through historic mining districts with views of the Sawatch Range.

stops.name: National Mining Hall of Fame and Museum
stops.detail: Learn about the silver boom and mineral history in one of the region's most comprehensive museums.

days.driving: Local town travel; allow for slower speeds due to high-altitude exertion.
days.note: Start physical activity early to avoid frequent afternoon mountain thunderstorms.

days.title: High Alpine Waters

stops.name: Turquoise Lake
stops.detail: Enjoy fishing or shoreline walks at this glacial reservoir surrounded by pine forest.

stops.name: Twin Lakes
stops.detail: Visit these natural lakes at the base of Independence Pass for kayaking or views of Mount Elbert.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for travel between Leadville and Twin Lakes; conditions vary with mountain weather.
days.note: Water temperatures are extremely cold; check for invasive species inspection requirements for watercraft.

days.title: Rocky Mountain Rails and Vistas

stops.name: Leadville, Colorado & Southern Railroad
stops.detail: Ride the historic train for views of the Arkansas River Valley and high-alpine scenery.

stops.name: Top of the Rockies Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive toward Independence Pass for high-altitude vistas, noting the seasonal road closure.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for scenic drive segments; Independence Pass is open summer only.
days.note: Independence Pass reaches 12,095 feet; ensure your vehicle and passengers are prepared for thin air.

intel.title: Town and Trailhead Access
intel.text: Street parking in downtown Leadville is generally available, but Mount Elbert trailheads fill by dawn during summer weekends. Plan for very early departures for peak hiking.

intel.title: High Country Dead Zones
intel.text: Service is reliable in town but disappears quickly on Independence Pass and remote forest roads. Carry physical maps for all backcountry navigation.

intel.title: Mountain Pass Prep
intel.text: Leadville serves as a primary fuel stop before Independence Pass. Verify levels before heading toward Aspen or remote mining districts.

intel.title: Acclimatization Window
intel.text: The 10,152-foot elevation requires adjustment; plan light activity for the first 24 hours. Hydration is essential to mitigate altitude symptoms.

intel.title: Seasonal Pass Closures
intel.text: Independence Pass (Hwy 82) closes annually for winter, typically from November to late May. Check CDOT for specific opening dates before planning a transit to Aspen.

plan.arrival: Pickup rental at Eagle County Regional Airport (EGE), shop for groceries in Buena Vista or Leadville, and allow time for altitude adjustment.
plan.vehicle: Check rental agreements for mountain pass driving; high-clearance vehicles are suggested for exploring historic mining roads.
plan.goldenHour: Harrison Avenue Historic District, with the Sawatch Range glowing at sunset, subject to mountain cloud cover.
